requirement:
CSS reports only `Comment` attachments. These include `/* … */` blocks and
`//` line comments recognized by the bundled CSS grammar.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.css.attachments` has two clauses. Neither is a structural obligation, so no implementation root is needed.

1. "CSS reports only `Comment` attachments." This restricts which attachment kinds appear in the output. An implementation could filter the kinds, or its extraction could only ever produce comments. Both give the same observable result, so the mechanism is discretionary.

2. "These include `/* … */` blocks and `//` line comments recognized by the bundled CSS grammar." This says which comment forms count as attachments. It does not prescribe a library, algorithm, signature, type or delegation. "Bundled CSS grammar" identifies which comments are recognized. Another scanner that recognized the same comments would produce identical output, so using the grammar is not a separate structural obligation.

The requirement has no `Implements` edges. It has one `Tests` edge (node 1896), which is the right kind of evidence for this behavioral text. I did not assess the adequacy of that test, since that belongs to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The requirement `requirements.sdk.sources.css.attachments` has two observable obligations. CSS must report only `Comment` attachments, and that set must include both `/* … */` blocks and `//` line comments.

`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` carries the `{test}` reference. Its `test.css` case uses the source `/* block */\na { color: red; }\n// line\n`. It gathers every attachment on every outline item and asserts the exact list of (kind, text) pairs: `[(Comment, "/* block */"), (Comment, "// line")]`.

- **Block comments:** the `/* block */` case is asserted to be a `Comment` with the right span.
- **Line comments:** the `// line` case is asserted the same way.
- **Only `Comment`:** the assertion compares the complete list, so any extra attachment, or any attachment of another kind such as `Annotation`, would fail it. The CSS rule `a { color: red; }` also yields no attachment, so the test checks that other syntax is not classified.

The requirement states no further boundaries, so I found no gaps.
